stem: Which inequality matches the sentence above?
stimulus: A sea turtle lays $n$ eggs in one nest. The number of eggs is at most $120$.
explanation: "At most 120" means 120 is the largest value allowed, and 120 itself is allowed. So $n$ can equal 120 or be less than it: $n \le 120$. In word-problem inequality questions, the limit words are usually what separates the answer choices. That makes this translation the first thing to practise.

B.why: You pointed the sign the wrong way. $n \ge 120$ means at least 120, so 120 would be the smallest number allowed. "At most" makes 120 the largest.

C.why: You read "at most" as "fewer than." The strict sign $<$ leaves out exactly 120 eggs, but "at most" allows 120. That is why the sign needs the bar underneath.

D.why: You wrote "more than 120," which is the opposite of the limit. Every value this choice allows is one the sentence rules out.

stem: Which inequality matches the sentence above?
stimulus: Today's high temperature was $18^{\circ}\text{C}$. Tonight's low temperature, $t$, in degrees Celsius, will be at most $6$ less than today's high.
explanation: "6 less than 18" means you start at 18 and take away 6, which gives $18 - 6$. "At most" gives $\le$. Together they make $t \le 18 - 6$. Harder questions put this same "k less than X" wording inside a longer expression, and the wrong choices swap the order of the subtraction.

A.why: You wrote the numbers in the order you read them. "6 less than 18" means 18 minus 6, not 6 minus 18. Your version gives $-12$ instead of $12$.

B.why: You got the subtraction right but used $\ge$. "At most" sets an upper limit, so the sign is $\le$.

D.why: You added the 6 instead of subtracting it. "Less than" means take away, so the limit is 6 degrees below 18, not 6 degrees above.

stem: Which inequality matches the sentence above?
stimulus: A heron's body length is $15$ centimeters. Its wingspan, $w$, in centimeters, is at least $2$ times its body length.
explanation: "2 times its body length" is $2(15)$. "At least" means this is the minimum, so the sign is $\ge$. That gives $w \ge 2(15)$. Word-problem inequalities often say "at least … times," and one wrong choice is usually the "maximum" version with the sign reversed.

A.why: You wrote a maximum when the sentence gives a minimum. "At least" means $w$ can be $2(15)$ or larger, so the sign is $\ge$.

C.why: You turned "2 times" into "plus 2." "Times" means multiply, so the minimum is $2(15) = 30$, not $15 + 2 = 17$.

D.why: You attached the 2 to the wrong quantity. The sentence doubles the body length, not the wingspan. Your version says half the wingspan is at least 15 cm, which is a different statement.

stem: Which inequality matches the sentence above?
stimulus: Each granola bar contains $8$ grams of sugar. The total sugar from $b$ granola bars can be no more than $32$ grams.
explanation: The total sugar is 8 grams for each bar times the number of bars, which is $8b$. "No more than" means $\le$. So the inequality is $8b \le 32$. This rate × count piece is the core of budget and cost questions, where a fixed fee is often added to it.

A.why: You used the right expression with the wrong sign. "No more than" sets an upper limit, so the sign is $\le$, not $\ge$.

B.why: You added the 8 grams once instead of multiplying it by the number of bars. Each bar adds 8 grams, so the total is $8b$, not $b + 8$.

C.why: You swapped the 8 and the 32. Each bar has 8 grams, and 32 grams is the limit. Your version puts the limit on the bars and the per-bar amount on the right.
